$comment: Cross-repo test vectors for SigningSession.descriptor_id / connect_vaults.fingerprint. Authoritative for coincube (desktop), keychain-app (Keychain), and coincube-api. Regenerated and asserted by coincube-gui/src/app/wallet.rs::descriptor_id_fingerprint_matches_committed_vectors — if you change this file, that test must still pass.

algorithm.name: descriptor_id_fingerprint
algorithm.definition: first 4 bytes of SHA-256 over the canonical descriptor string's UTF-8 bytes, rendered as 8 lowercase hex characters
algorithm.preimage: the descriptor exactly as rust-miniscript's Display emits it — which is also exactly the plaintext sealed into SigningSession.descriptor_envelopes
algorithm.signer_rule: A signer MUST hash the decrypted descriptor_envelopes plaintext verbatim. Do not re-parse, re-serialise, normalise, or strip the '#checksum' before hashing. Never interpret descriptor_id itself as a descriptor.

canonicalisation.checksum: The 8-character '#checksum' suffix is ALWAYS part of the hashed bytes. CoincubeDescriptor's Display forwards to the inner multipath descriptor with a hard-coded non-alternate write!, so miniscript's write_checksum_if_not_alt gate can never be bypassed — even format!("{:#}", desc) carries the checksum. An input with the checksum omitted has it re-appended by parse -> to_string before hashing, so it yields the SAME id.
canonicalisation.multipath: A multipath key '<a;b>' is preserved verbatim and in written order. It is NOT expanded into separate receive/change descriptors before hashing; only the multipath descriptor is ever hashed.
canonicalisation.key_order: Keys are hashed exactly as written. Nothing is sorted. Swapping two keys inside multi() produces a DIFFERENT descriptor_id (see vector multipath_2of2_keys_swapped). sortedmulti cannot arise: CoincubeDescriptor rejects it at parse.
canonicalisation.hardened_markers: 'h' hardened markers are normalised to "'" by Display, so the two spellings share one id.
canonicalisation.origin_fingerprint_case: Origin fingerprint hex is lowercased by Display.
canonicalisation.whitespace: Whitespace inside a descriptor is a parse error; inputs are trimmed at the UI edge before parsing.

vectors.name: multipath_2of2_with_checksum
vectors.note: Baseline: 2-of-2 primary path plus a single-key recovery path behind older(3).

vectors.name: multipath_2of2_checksum_stripped
vectors.note: PROVES checksum handling: same descriptor as the baseline with '#p9ax3xxp' removed from the input. Display re-appends it, so the preimage and the id are identical to the baseline. A signer that hashes the stripped form gets a different id and is wrong.

vectors.name: multipath_2of2_keys_swapped
vectors.note: PROVES key order is significant: the baseline's two multi() keys are swapped. Nothing re-sorts them, so the canonical form takes a different checksum (#9f7e4449) and the vault gets a DIFFERENT id.

vectors.name: multipath_2of2_h_hardened
vectors.note: PROVES hardened-marker normalisation: the baseline written with 'h' instead of apostrophes. Display normalises to apostrophes, so the id matches the baseline exactly.

vectors.name: singlesig_timelock_with_checksum
vectors.note: A second real policy shape: single primary key with a timelocked recovery key.

rejected.name: sortedmulti
rejected.note: ANSWERS 'are keys reordered before hashing?': they are not, because sortedmulti never reaches the hash. CoincubeDescriptor::from_str rejects it — CoincubePolicy::from_multipath_descriptor accepts only WshInner::Ms, not WshInner::SortedMulti. A signer receiving a sortedmulti descriptor should refuse it rather than attempt to canonicalise key order.
rejected.error_contains: not compatible with a Coincube spending policy
